arguments.title: COM459 Japan shot direction
arguments.message:
I'm the video editor for ComfortWear. Please DIRECT this ad: for every line of the VO tell me exactly which scene goes on screen and what text goes where. I will source and cut the footage.

## The ad: COM459 (Travel/JAPAN iteration of our winner COM376 "Worst shoes for Disney"; sister ad COM458 = NYC, already cut and approved)
Execution: Mash-Up. Our ads perform best when the B-roll is ORGANIC UGC of the exact place being talked about. For Japan that means real phone footage of Tokyo/Kyoto/Osaka: subway & station stairs, Shinjuku/Shibuya station crowds, packed rush-hour trains, ramen/food lines, museum floors, Fushimi Inari / temple stone steps, shrines, wet station tiles, Japan winter snow, Shinjuku night alleys (Omoide Yokocho / Golden Gai), last train, step counters, tired travelers on benches. Sourced from TikTok. Product scenes from our own ComfortWear Ortho Stretch footage (knit slip-on sneaker, wide toe box, stretch knit, arch insole, orange/black slip-resistant outsole). AI shots available: AI podiatrist "Dr. Moore, DPM" (lab coat, clinic) lip-synced to the VO, 3D foot-in-shoe animations with red pressure glow (foam packing flat / toes crushed).

## PACING RULES (new, from analysing our $20k+ spend ads — the client said COM458 changed scenes too fast)
- One scene per ~5 words of VO (median shot ~1.8 s); no shot under ~1.2 s except a deliberate quick burst.
- Each shot = ONE continuous take (never a clip that has the creator's own jump-cuts inside it).
- Keep a scene on screen across a whole short phrase rather than cutting on every noun; group consecutive related nouns into one shot when they're < 1.2 s apart.
So please plan ~ (VO words / 5) shots, not a cut per noun.

## Hooks (3 variants, shared body)
Hook 1 VO: Hokas and On Clouds are the worst shoes you can pack for Japan. I know that'll upset people, but it is not the brand. It is the design. | Super: Hokas & On Clouds are the WORST shoes for Japan ❌
Hook 2 VO: If you're packing Hokas or On Clouds for Japan because someone called them the best walking shoes, take them out of your suitcase right now. | Super: STOP packing Hokas and On Clouds for Japan 🛑
Hook 3 VO: The biggest mistake travelers make before flying to Japan is packing $160 running shoes like Hokas or On Clouds. You think you bought the ultimate walking shoe, but you're setting yourself up for wrecked feet by day two. | Super: The #1 footwear mistake travelers make in Japan ✈️

## Body (VO | Super)
P1: These shoes are built to move a runner forward for forty minutes, not for someone walking twenty-five thousand steps across Japan. When you are exploring Tokyo, Kyoto, or Osaka, you are not just taking a casual stroll. You are climbing five flights of subway stairs, walking miles across concrete train stations, standing on packed trains, and navigating hard pavement for eight, nine, sometimes ten hours straight. Three things people overlook until they are already thousands of miles from home. | Super: 20,000+ steps every day in Japan 🚶‍♂️
P2: Number one, that soft cushioning in the store does not tell you the whole story. Hokas use thick, squishy foam designed to bounce a runner forward on a flat road. But in Japan, you spend hours standing on crowded trains, waiting in line for food, and standing on museum floors. That soft foam packs completely flat under your body weight. And On Clouds use hollow pods that compress under constant pressure. Once that cushioning flattens out, your arches sink, leaving you with zero support right when your feet have miles left to walk. | Super: 1. Soft foam packs flat while standing 📉
P3: Number two, Hokas and On Clouds were not built for city hazards and winter weather. In Japan, you are constantly walking across polished subway tiles, metal train grates, and steep stone temple steps. And with winter here, those surfaces get wet, slick, and covered in patches of ice or snow. The massive soles on Hokas make your feet unstable, wobbling over every curb and putting strain on your knees. And the smooth, hollow pods on On Clouds offer almost no grip on slick wet floors. One slip on an icy train entrance or wet tile staircase can end your trip on day one. That is where a slip-resistant outsole matters. You need real grip, not an unstable running platform. | Super: 2. Dangerous on slick tiles, ice & snow ❄️
P4: Number three, the toe box is narrow, and the upper does not stretch. Both Hokas and On Clouds are built with rigid, tapered toe boxes meant to lock a runner's foot in place. But after walking twenty thousand steps on hard concrete, your feet naturally swell. When your toes get crammed together with nowhere to go, that friction leads to burning arches, blisters, and throbbing nerve pain. If your shoes feel tight by lunch, you are loosening your laces on a bench outside a shrine when you still have half your day to go. | Super: 3. Narrow toe boxes crush swelling feet 🦶
P5: That is why Comfortwear built the exact opposite of an athletic running shoe. They did not design it for marathon runners. They built it for people whose feet have to survive real life: nurses, healthcare workers, and travelers who want to actually enjoy the trip they spent years saving for. A roomy, wide toe box lets your toes spread out naturally so you stay balanced. A flexible stretch knit upper gives your feet breathing room as they swell throughout the day. And built-in structural arch support holds your feet firm hour after hour, paired with a slip-resistant outsole that grips slick station tiles, wet pavement, and winter slush. | Super: Built for real travel, not 40-minute runs ✅
P6: Because you flew all the way to Japan to make memories, not to sit in your hotel room icing your feet at three in the afternoon. You do not want to be the person limping behind, telling everyone else to go ahead without you while you look for somewhere to sit. You want to be in every photo, climbing to the top of the shrine, exploring the night alleys in Shinjuku, and still feeling great when the last train runs. | Super: Don't let sore feet cut your dream trip short 🇯🇵
P7: Right now, for the Holiday Sale, Comfortwear is up to forty percent off with free shipping, which puts them under sixty dollars a pair. Plus, you get thirty days to try them risk-free. Order a pair and put them through your longest walking days at home before you fly out. If they do not keep your feet completely supported and pain-free, send them back. Tap below and grab your pair before the Holiday Sale ends and before you pack for Japan. | Super: Holiday Sale: Up to 40% Off + 30-Day Guarantee 🎁

## What I need back (write it to a markdown file in outputs and summarise in the answer)
1. Text system: which supers become the hook card / numbered section headlines / offer stickers vs. which stay as running captions only (COM376 & our approved COM458 used: hook card, '#1 - ...' section headlines, running caption pills, offer stickers + end card; no feature pills/banners).
2. For each hook and body part: a shot table: shot #, exact VO words it covers (start..end words), visual description, source tier (JAPAN_UGC / COMPETITOR_UGC / PRODUCT / AI / ANIMATION), TikTok search query for UGC shots.
3. Where the AI podiatrist appears in each hook and body.
4. Top 20 TikTok search queries for the Japan UGC.
